subject: Clarify: compute locality, vendor chain, and POC data handling
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@nutriplan.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Walker <t.walker@nutriplan.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick Q before POC: where will requests run and who else sees them?

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the POC looks promising. Before we spin up a workload, a couple of quick questions from legal/IT: where exactly will the LLM inference for our POC execute (region/by-cloud), and do you have a list of any third-party subprocessors that could see payloads in transit or at rest?

Specifically:
- Can you confirm the cloud regions (US/EU) used by the hosted POC?
- Any transient hops through partner networks or analytics vendors?
- Retention: how long do request logs / KV caches persist for the POC?

If you can send a one-page summary + vendor roster we can pass to infosec. Appreciate it —

Sofia Ramos
Head of IT, NutriPlan Labs
S: (415) 555-0132

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@nutriplan.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q before POC: where will requests run and who else sees them?

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: for the POC we can constrain execution to US-only regions and provide a current subprocessor roster. Longer details and evidence attached.

Key points:
- Region: POC will be provisioned in our us-west-2 cluster by default; we can pin to any single US region for the test (us-east-1 or us-west-2). No EU/APAC hops unless you request cross-region routing.
- Subprocessors: runtime compute and storage are our hosted clusters + two subcontracts: CloudOps (managed host) and Observability Inc (log aggregation). Both are listed in the attached roster with contact points and SOC 2 status.
- Transient hops: customer request path -> load balancer -> inference pool -> optional metrics pipeline. Metrics are routed to Observability Inc; payloads are not routed to external NLP vendors.
- Retention: request metadata and tracing: 30 days by default for POC; model KV caches are ephemeral (auto-evicted within session) and are not persisted beyond the instance lifecycle. We can set shorter retention on request metadata if needed.

Attachments:
- redwood-regional-ops-map.pdf (summary diagram of routing + region constraints)
- subprocessor_roster_2027-04.csv (company, role, compliance attestation)

Marissa/Karthik — looping you in for any technical proof points or auditor contacts if they request evidence.

Next step: Sofia, would you prefer us to: (A) run the POC in us-west-2 and provide tailored retention limits, or (B) provide an isolated Dedicated trial?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (510) 555-0202

From: Tom Walker <t.walker@nutriplan.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T15:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q before POC: where will requests run and who else sees them?

Jordan — thanks, that helps. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/security:

1) Can you confirm whether Observability Inc receives full request payloads or only anonymized telemetry? We need that for our dataflow diagram.
2) Is there an option to disable metrics export entirely for the POC? (We'd rather collect nothing than share anything externally.)
3) For the subprocessor roster CSV, do you have contract dates and a point of contact for audit requests?

If you can reply with those items and any short evidence (SOC 2 snapshot, contractual MSA references) we can move the POC forward this week.

Thanks,
Tom Walker
Director, Procurement — NutriPlan Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Walker <t.walker@nutriplan.com>, Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@nutriplan.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T16:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q before POC: where will requests run and who else sees them?

Tom/Sofia — quick clarifications from the compliance side:

1) Observability Inc only receives aggregated telemetry and hashed request IDs by default; full request bodies are NOT forwarded. We segregate logs so raw payloads remain in our primary cluster storage unless an admin-enabled export is requested under a support ticket.
2) Yes — we can disable metrics export for the POC. There is a toggle at the instance level; we'll ship a POC config with metrics_export=false.
3) The attached subprocessor_roster_2027-04.csv includes contract start dates and SOC 2 scope. For audit requests we surface evidence via our compliance portal (link above) or we can provide PDF snapshots: SOC 2 report (redacted) and a copy of the subprocessor agreement.

Short procedural note: If NutriPlan wants an extra assurance, we can enable customer-side KMS for any stored artifacts and provide a one-week retention window for request logs. That would be a sensible middle ground for a production pilot.

I'll attach the SOC 2 snapshot and the redwood-regional-ops-map.pdf to this thread (both included).

Next steps: Jordan will push a POC config (us-west-2, metrics_export=false, retention=7d) and provide the HubSpot record with the audit items.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0333

Attachments referenced:
- SOC2-redwood-2027-redacted.pdf (attached)
- redwood-regional-ops-map.pdf (attached)
